reason: The two quotes recommend DynamoDB for serverless apps needing consistent low latency, automatic scaling and no complex joins or transactions, and call RDS a better choice for complex SQL queries, joins or existing relational applications.

The quotes give the parallelization factor from 1 (default) to 10 for concurrent batches per shard, and state that within a shard records sharing a partition key go to the same batch and are processed in order.
The quote states Lambda polls DynamoDB stream shards at a base rate of 4 times per second.
The quote names an SQS FIFO queue or SNS FIFO topic as an unsupported destination type and says Lambda then sends a DestinationDeliveryFailures metric to CloudWatch.
The quote states each function can have multiple destinations, separate for success and failure, configurable on a function, function version or alias.
The quote states separate destinations for success and failure, a standard SQS queue or SNS topic as dead-letter queue, and that a DLQ receives only the event content without response details.
The quota row gives 3,000 durable operations per durable execution and says it cannot be increased.
The quote lists charges for durable operations, data written (GB) and retention (GB-month, prorated); the context says existing Lambda compute charges also apply.
The quota row gives 5,000,000 per Region, 10,000,000 in the three named Regions, and calls it a soft limit that can be increased.
The quota row gives 100 MB cumulative payload persisted per execution and says it cannot be increased.

The quote says durable functions are cost-effective for wait-heavy workflows with no compute charges during waits, and Fargate fits workloads needing continuous compute; the context frames it as long-running workloads.

The two quotes state durable functions are for application development in Lambda tightly coupled with business logic, and Step Functions for orchestration across AWS services with visual design, 220+ integrations and zero maintenance.

The quote is the ** note under the 'Provisioned Concurrency Pricing' heading (the only occurrence on the page), but the claim states it for all functions; the SnapStart page says init code is billed 'For SnapStart functions', so the general scope is not supported.

The sentence sits in the 'Provisioned Concurrency Pricing' paragraph (the only occurrence on the page) and describes duration for Provisioned Concurrency; the claim drops that scope and states it for all functions.

The quotes state event-driven apps communicate across networks and introduce variable latency, and that consistent low-latency workloads such as HFT or sub-millisecond robotics are not good candidates.
The quote supports polling inefficiency and webhook limits, but the context says both mechanisms 'can be replaced by events'; the claim states as fact that 'events replace both'.
The table row lists viewer request and viewer response for CloudFront Functions, and those plus origin request and origin response for Lambda@Edge.
The table row shows Network access: No for CloudFront Functions and Yes for Lambda@Edge.
Under Lambda@Edge Pricing, the quote states the monthly request price is $0.60 per 1 million requests.
The quotes require a mount target in every AZ the function connects to, at least two AZs for performance and resilience, and NFS port 2049 allowed by the function and mount target security groups.

The quotes state that with a user-configured IAM policy the role needs elasticfilesystem permissions, included in AmazonElasticFileSystemClientReadWriteAccess, plus permissions to connect to the file system's VPC.
The quotes state a function can mount EFS to a local directory to access and modify shared resources safely at high concurrency, connecting over the local network in a VPC.
The quote lists the four resources Lambda always encrypts at rest: environment variables, uploaded files incl. deployment packages and layers, ESM filter criteria, durable execution data.
The quota row gives 3,000 ENIs per VPC, adjustable Yes, and says Lambda creates a network interface for each subnet and security group combination.
The quota row gives default 3,000, can be increased up to 'Thousands', and says the quota is shared with other services such as Amazon EFS.
The quota row gives 4 KB for all environment variables associated with the function, in aggregate.
The quote supports termination every few hours even for continuously invoked functions, but says 'You should not assume'; the claim strengthens it to 'you must not assume'.
The quote states 512 MB is available to each function at no additional cost and you pay only for additional storage; the context says cost depends on amount and execution duration.
In Example 3 of the Ephemeral Storage Pricing section, whose examples are stated to use US East (N. Virginia) prices, the quote gives $0.0000000309 per GB-second with 512 MB free.

The quote is from a pricing example; the same section says an SQS ESM EPU supports one event poller and a Kafka EPU a default of 10, so 'each supporting 10 event pollers' drops the Kafka condition and the example scope.
The quote states ESMs process each event at least once, duplicate processing can occur, and function code should be idempotent.
The quotes list the three criteria (batching window maximum, batch size met, payload reaches 6 MB) and state the 6 MB limit cannot be modified.
The quote and context state Kinesis and SQS use an ESM instead of a trigger, which polls, batches records and invokes the function with the batch.
The quotes give a 0-second default for Kinesis, DynamoDB and SQS (invoke as soon as records are available) and a configurable range of 0 to 300 seconds in 1-second increments.
The quote states Lambda actively fetches (pulls) events from a queue or stream and handles polling and invocation, in contrast to services that push events.
The quote states service errors or throttles that do not reach the function do not count toward retry attempts, and an ESM can send an invocation record to a destination when it discards a batch.
The quote states the default reprocessing of the entire batch until success or expiry, the pause of the affected shard for in-order processing, and configurable retries for DynamoDB and Kinesis.
The quote defines an event as anything that triggers a function and names direct invocation (push) and event source mappings (pull); the context says ESMs pull from a queue or stream.
The quote states that as a best practice, before publishing to production, the policy should include only the required permissions.
The quote states every function must have an execution role with at least CloudWatch access because functions log to CloudWatch Logs by default, satisfied by AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole.
